thread.title: Salty Snacks, Sweeter Returns - PepsiCo Inc. (NYSE:PEP)

author: AllStarTrader
title: Salty Snacks, Sweeter Returns - PepsiCo Inc. (NYSE:PEP)
text:
Dividend Hike Pepsico was a recent addition into my portfolio. With the pullback under $100 I could no longer resist the tempting high yield. For years I have wanted to get add this stalwart to the portfolio as a long term holding, but never found the right time to add. Well the starts aligned and I had cash ready to deploy.With the recent dividend raise, PEP was yield a historically high yield of close to 3.8% at $98 per share.
Source: Seeking Alpha
This marks the 46th year of dividend increases from Pepsico. There is also nothing stopping Pepsico from continuing its increases as the payout ratio is at a respectable 65% of forward earnings estimates of $5.70. This compares favorably to Coca Kola's payout ratio. KO is paying a 2018 dividend of $1.56 per share and earning an estimated 2.08. That equates to a 75% payout ratio, which may be white KO has not announced a double digit increase to the dividend like PEP.
We also see below that PEP is well capitalized and in no danger of having a dividend cut.
Source: TD Ameritrade
Share Buybacks We also saw a newly announced share repurchase program, giving even more cash back to investors. This buyback is set to expire in June of 2021. It should be noted that at current market valuations Pepsi only has a $150B market cap, so $15B in share repurchases is close to 10% of the company's shares outstanding. The last program for $12B, ran from 2015 until 2018. In fact from 2005 to 2018 we see about 300 million shares have been repurchased.
Source: Macrotrends
With 20% of the outstanding shares being repurchased in the past 15 years and another 10% being repurchased in the next 3, Pepsi has made long term share holders effectively own 30% more of the company in less then 20 years.
Repatriation Something I haven't seen or heard an announcement on was plans for repatriating money from overseas. Pepsi has a huge international presence and stands to benefit from the recent tax change. Whether the cash is used for acquisitions or to deleverage, all can be positives for the company and its growth going forward. From what I have found, PEP holds close to $20 Billion in cash over seas. This is among the largest of overseas cash hoards in corporate America.
Source: USA Today
[Note: that this is total cash on hand, abroad and domestic] $15B of Pepsi's cash is estimated to be abroad. Whatever Pepsico decides, as long as it is put to use and not left idle will be a net positive for shareholders and the company.
Health and Growth Below are the "Good for You" and "Better for You" brands as Pepsi has labeled it.
Source: Pepsi Brands
Pepsi has not been ignoring the change to healthy snacks and beverages. The management team has been smart enough to use the large and stable cash flows from the core businesses to invest in new products, segments, and acquisitions. Just last month, Pepsi announced it would be acquiring Bare Snacks. While the terms of the agreement were not disclosed, this is another a perfect tuck in acquisition for the company. Pepsi can use its distribution network to offer grocery stores, convenience stores, sports complexes, and vending routes another healthy snack alternative. The power of its distribution network really makes the small company purchases very beneficial. Most of the time smaller companies are unable to get into many of the large chains or C-Stores as the competition is intense. PEP , is able to take these small distributors of healthy snacks and expand their presence immensely, growing revenues and profitability, while generating high ROI. And not only are they focusing on snacks, in late 2016 they acquired Kevita , a maker of probiotic sparkling drinks. And not only do they acquire brands, they start them. As we have seen with the announcement of a recent launch, Bubbly, only one year after launching Life Water. Recently bottled water over took carbonated drinks as the top seller in the United States, but sparkling water is on a tear as well. More information can on this trend can found here . Competitor National Beverage has seen exploding growth and trades at a loft valuation for having just one big brand.
FIZZ PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts
FIZZ , maker of La Croix trades multiples above PEP and relies on revenue from one product. Granted the growth is great, but Pepsi has multiple sparkling beverage products and a larger customer foot print. While we cannot see the growth PEP is seeing specifically in sparkling as numbers are not provided, we can presume it is growing quickly.
With the combination of acquisitions and product launches, Pepsi now generates about 50% of its revenue from healthy snacks and beverages. I believe this will grow increasingly important as more and more consumers become health conscious and look for more nutritious alternatives.
Dividends I like being paid for the investments I make. I find that as an owner of a company, you should entitled to the profits. I like dividends not only as a source of income, but as a return on my investment. Pepsico has shown a strong commitment to shareholders by increasing their ownership in the company and returning profits to their pockets.
PEP data by YCharts
You can now purchase PEP with the highest yield it has had in 10 years and the lower forward multiple average than in the past year.
PEP Dividend Yield (NYSE: TTM ) data by YCharts
The chart above shows the trailing yield and not the current yield. I included it to show in the past 10 years. There has not been a time where the dividend yield was above 3.7%.
Conclusion The chance to add a consumer staple company at 52 week lows, with the market near highs is often rare. While Pepsi may not be the fast grower it once was, I believe it will continue to diversify its revenue stream into healthier snacks and beverages. By focusing on proven products within small companies, I believe Pepsi is able to create enormous value out of their acquisitions. I also believe they are keeping watch on current market trends, as creating new products has shown they have done. I find it fair to acquire PEP at $105 or less, as this is a an approximate p/e of 18.4 on forward earnings and below its historical average. Regardless, a stalwart like PEP can always find a spot in my portfolio and should shares remain depressed I will continue to add them to my portfolio.
Disclosure: I am/we are long PEP, T, O, STOR, JCAP, KIM, BIT, AAPL, FDX, FB, OI, AQN, ABBV, JD, V, PRU, JNJ.
